label: copy phase: input i when the output is 0 (or a repeated i), i.e. recalling an original "i 0" / "i i" bigram
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only (99.7% of mass) when the fed-back input is the letter i. Within those steps it is selective for what is output next: out_tok = 0 (original bigram "i 0") carries 75% of the mass and the largest activations (top examples are all "i 0"), and out_tok = i (bigram "i i") carries 18% at weaker magnitude. It is near-silent at recall_idx 0-2 and strongest for recall_idx 3-4 / later timesteps. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and not on i followed by other tokens. Precision is incomplete: about a third of predicted i->0/i steps are inactive, with no visible difference from active ones (some "i i" cases with no 0 following are off), and about 10% of mass is weak firing on i followed by other letters or at early recall positions.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, 0, -, y, z, v; least: w, t, a, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: 0, i, a, m, g, h; least: p, k, t, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=9 & t=13.
